In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Enterprise Core Account Executive, UK
descriptionHtml:

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Are you a high-achieving sales professional ready to digitally transform the physical operations that power our planet? As a Strategic AE you will be helping large mid-market and enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

title: Executive Director, Clinical Research - Neurodegeneration
descriptionHtml:
Overview

Alnylam Pharmaceuticals is seeking an imaginative physician drug developer. This is an opportunity to provide clinical leadership in developing RNAi therapeutics in Alnylam’s rapidly expanding portfolio, which spans the areas of rare genetic diseases, cardio-metabolic diseases, neuroscience, hematology and hepatology.

The successful candidate’s primary role will be to drive the pipeline forward through leadership of clinical development programs.  While the primary focus responsibility will be as clinical lead physician on Alnylam’s Huntington’s program, the role may support across a range of therapeutic areas and all stages of development may be required as pipeline assets evolve. The Executive Director is expected to play a leading and influencing role in the overall clinical development strategies and drive progress and operational excellence for associated clinical trials. In addition, this role will include interaction with Alnylam’s research group, helping to advise the team on the clinical development feasibility of novel targets and the design of proof-of-concept studies. This work will also involve extensive consultation and collaboration with external experts. It is expected that additional opportunities will arise to lead bench-to-bedside early phase clinical development programs.

The Executive Director, Clinical Research, will work in a matrix organization across Regulatory, Biostatistics, Clinical Operations, Preclinical, Commercial & QA teams to ensure fully harmonized and integrated development strategies. They will be a key Alnylam Development spokesperson at external meetings, including regulatory interactions and scientific meetings.

This position is hybrid, requiring weekly onsite presence and will be primarily located at our Cambridge, MA headquarters or Maidenhead, UK location. Relocation may be possible for the selected candidate.

Key Responsibilities

  • Be the strategic leader providing a strong, clear voice for the clinical programs
  • Develop creative but realistic approaches to drug development and lead clinical efforts to secure global regulatory approvals
  • Oversight of trial conduct and safety
  • Provide strategic consultation and guidance to Research on all decisions that have significant clinical components and implications. 
  • Collaborate closely with Preclinical, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs and Commercial to ensure tight strategic integration of product development plans
  • Be accountable via Clinical Research and Operations for all relevant timelines and deliverables
  • Drive/supervise all major written deliverables (regulatory submissions, original articles, abstracts), and presentation materials
  • Be responsible (as appropriate in line with SOPs) for final review and sign off with respect to all controlled documents including protocols, IBs, informed consent forms
  • Influence internal and external audiences in a high impact, highly visible fashion

Qualifications

  • MD with strong research background or MD PhD, with a track record of successful research support and peer review publications. Board Certification (or equivalent) or specialist training is highly desirable; drug development experience in neurology (Huntington’s Disease) would be a great advantage, but not essential
  • 10+ years industry experience or equivalent clinical academic experience
  • Sound scientific and clinical judgment
  • Successful track record of leading Phase 2/3 clinical programs (preferably in Huntington’s drug development), including major interactions with Health Authorities
  • Familiarity with concepts of clinical research and clinical trial design, including biostatistics, regulatory agency organization, guidelines, and practices
  • Ability to effectively present ideas and document complex medical/clinical concepts in both written and oral communication
  • History of solving problems while exhibiting superior judgment and a balanced, realistic understanding of issues
  • Outstanding leadership and collaboration skills working within a matrix environment.
  • Experience and knowledge of working with biotech/pharma partner(s) a plus
  • Thrives in highly entrepreneurial biotech environment and embraces Alnylam’s culture of science, passion and urgency.

title: Financial Controller (w/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Tangany mit Sitz in München ist ein innovatives Technologieunternehmen mit einer marktführenden B2B-Lösung für die Verwahrung digitaler Vermögenswerte (z. B. Kryptowährungen, Stablecoins und anderen tokenisierten Vermögenswerten) in Blockchain-Netzwerken. Unsere Lösung wird bereits von mehr als 50 institutionellen Kunden eingesetzt. Als lizenziertes Finanzinstitut wird die Tangany GmbH von der BaFin reguliert.

Für unser anhaltendes Wachstum suchen wir einen Financial Controller (w/m/d) zur Verstärkung unseres Teams.

Deine Rolle

Du verantwortest das Controlling und die Finanzsteuerung und berichtest an das Management Board.

Das Team ist klein. Deine Expertise und dein Beitrag wirken sich unmittelbar aus: Du arbeitest mit unserer Accountant und unserer Steuerkanzlei z.B. an Themen wie Finanzbuchhaltung, Lohn und Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung; die formale Verantwortung für das Rechnungswesen liegt bei der Geschäftsleitung, Zahlungen geben wir im Vier-Augen-Prinzip frei. In diesem Rahmen bist du die Person, die weiß, wo die Zahlen stehen, warum sie dort stehen und wie sich Ergebnis, Kosten, Liquidität und Eigenmittel entwickeln werden.

Der Kern der Rolle hat zwei Seiten: die regulatorische Pflicht und eine Steuerung, mit der wir jede Finanzfrage jederzeit in wenigen Minuten beantworten können. Business Cases und Investor Reporting kommen dazu und wachsen mit dir.

Heute arbeiten wir vor allem mit DATEV Unternehmen Online und Tableau. Die Steuerung darauf baust du zu großen Teilen neu auf, gern AI-gestützt: Unser AI-Dev-Team setzt mit dir Live-Reporting, Abstimmungen und ein Finanz-Cockpit um.

Aufgaben

  • Den Jahresabschluss nach HGB und RechKredV erstellen, ergänzt um die RechZahlV-Posten für unser Zahlungsgeschäft, und die Prüfung gemeinsam mit unserer Steuerkanzlei und Abschlussprüfer durchführen.

  • Das aufsichtsrechtliche Meldewesen führen und Finanzinformationen nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben unter Begleitung des Compliance-Teams bereitstellen.

  • Regulatorische Planzahlen, etwa die Eigenmittelanforderung, aus der Bilanzplanung ableiten und in Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsleitung laufend überwachen.

  • Cashflow- und Runway-Planung führen und Finanzierungsbedarf früh sichtbar machen.

  • Liquiditäts- und Kontrahentenrisiken in das unternehmensweite Risikocontrolling einbringen und laufend überwachen.

  • Business Cases und Rentabilitätsrechnungen erstellen und Investor-Updates vorbereiten.

  • Eine Kostenstellenstruktur aufbauen, Budgets je Kostenstelle mit den Verantwortlichen festlegen, Kosten, Budgets und KPIs laufend überwachen sowie Live-Reporting und Ad-hoc-Auswertungen für Geschäftsleitung und Budgetverantwortliche bereitstellen und Plan-Ist-Abweichungen analysieren.

  • Aus der Praxiserfahrung heraus Input liefern, um Finanzprozesse, Tools und das interne Kontrollsystem gemeinsam mit unserem AI-Dev-Team auszubauen.

Wen wir suchen

  • Du bist Controller:in (idealerweise aus einem regulierten Institut) und hast Jahresabschluss und Meldewesen selbst verantwortet.

  • Abweichungen erkennst du früh: Wenn sich Eigenmittel, Liquidität oder Kosten in die falsche Richtung bewegen, liegt deine Analyse mit Optionen auf dem Tisch, solange noch Zeit zum Handeln ist.

  • Deine Forecasts halten auch Monate später, und wo sie abweichen, kannst du erklären, warum.

  • Meldefristen und Prüfungsanforderungen baust du so in die Abläufe ein, dass vor dem Stichtag keine Ad-hoc Aktion nötig ist.

  • Prüfer und Risikocontrolling nehmen deine Zahlen als Ausgangspunkt.

  • Stellt die Geschäftsleitung eine Finanzfrage, kannst du schnell und problemlos Antworten geben, weil deine Daten und Auswertungen genau dafür gebaut sind.

  • Offenheit: Reporting mit AI-Werkzeugen neu aufsetzen.

Reporting to the VP Finance, you will lead initiatives that improve the effectiveness, efficiency and scalability of Finance through process redesign, technology enablement, data governance and operational excellence.

This role sits at the intersection of finance operations, systems, data and business performance. You will be responsible for transforming core finance processes, improving controls, implementing enabling technologies and ensuring that transformation initiatives deliver measurable and sustainable business value.

Unlike a traditional programme management role, success will not be measured solely by project delivery. You will be expected to challenge assumptions, validate outcomes and ensure that process and system changes translate into tangible improvements in close efficiency, reporting quality, control effectiveness and decision-making.

You will play a key role in consolidating information from a diverse systems landscape, improving data quality and governance, and helping establish a single source of truth for financial and operational reporting.

What you’ll bring.

Finance Process Transformation & Operational Excellence

  • Assist in the design and implementation of the Finance Target Operating Model (TOM), covering processes, systems and data, providing input and recommendations to support the overall TOM design.

  • Develop and maintain a transformation roadmap aligned to business objectives, operational efficiency, governance requirements and future compliance needs, including SOX readiness.

  • Analyse and redesign finance processes to improve productivity, control effectiveness and user experience.

  • Identify control gaps, operational risks and process inefficiencies, developing practical and prioritised remediation plans.

  • Establish robust data governance, validation and reporting frameworks to improve the quality, consistency and reliability of financial information.

  • Map and optimise end-to-end transaction flows across multiple systems and data sources.

  • Support the creation of scalable reporting and analytics capabilities that provide meaningful operational and financial insight.

Finance Systems & Automation

  • Lead finance systems and automation projects from initial requirements through to implementation and post-go-live stabilisation.

  • Partner with Finance and Technology teams to evaluate, select and implement solutions that support future-state finance operations.

  • Drive automation opportunities across close processes, journal management, reconciliations, variance analysis and reporting.

  • Ensure data integrity, auditability and control considerations are embedded within all system and process changes.

title: Forward Deployed Architect
descriptionHtml:
Who We Are

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About the Role:

As a Forward Deployed Architect on Notion’s Services team, you will help customers turn AI ambition into operational reality and unlock the full potential of our platform. You will partner directly with customers to design, build, and launch AI-native workflows that drive adoption, usage, and measurable business outcomes.

This role sits at the center of Notion’s workflow-led GTM motion. You will partner directly with customers to understand their business goals, operating processes, technical environment, governance needs, and adoption barriers, then translate that context into scalable Notion architectures that drive measurable value.

You will be hands-on across discovery, solution design, workspace architecture, workflow build, AI implementation, launch planning, adoption and handoff. You will work deeply with customers to define what Notion should own, where it should integrate with existing systems, and how Notion can become a durable operating layer for their teams.

The best candidates combine strong consultative discovery, systems thinking, technical fluency, AI-native workflow design, implementation judgment and exceptional customer presence. You should be comfortable reasoning through technical tradeoffs, designing scalable solutions, and partnering closely with Forward Deployed Engineering when deeper engineering support is required.

 

What You'll Achieve:

  • Hands-on AI builder mindset, with experience using AI tools to design, prototype, automate, or improve real business workflows.

  • Technical fluency with APIs, integrations, data models, automation, enterprise systems, developer workflows and implementation tradeoffs. You do not need to write production code but you should be able to reason through technical constraints and troubleshoot effectively.

  • Strong experience delivering implementations that drive adoption, change management and long-term customer value.

  • Strong project and engagement management skills, including ownership of scope, timeline, deliverables, stakeholder alignment, risks, decisions, dependencies and launch readiness.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts for business, technical, and executive audiences.

  • Strong executive presence and customer judgment, with the ability to build trust, frame tradeoffs clearly, and move ambiguous decisions forward.

  • Bias toward action, high learning velocity, and comfort building in fast-changing AI-native product environments.

 

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience designing or deploying Agents, automations or AI-powered workflows with Customers.

  • Experience with Notion, APIs, MCPs, Workers, coding agents or developer platform workflows.

  • Experience developing discovery methodologies, reusable delivery assets, internal tooling, packaged services or reference architectures from the ground up.

  • Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams to turn field learnings into roadmap signal, reusable architecture patterns or scalable product improvements.

  • Previous experience in a fast-paced, high-growth technology environment.

Du arbeitest direkt mit den Gründern, näher dran geht nicht. Founder Associate heißt bei uns: Du bist die Feuerwehr. Wo es brennt, bist du zuerst da, egal ob Investor-Update, Prototypen-Logistik oder der Messestand am Freitag.

Melde dich, wenn:

title: Founders Associate Intern (m/w/d) - Hybrid
descriptionHtml:
PatientFirst Fertility baut eine der ambitioniertesten digital-first Gruppen moderner IVF-Kliniken im Privatzahlersegment - mit klarer Skalierungslogik und schlankem HQ. Die erste Klinik ist live und profitabel. Jetzt kommt die Phase, in der aus einer Klinik eine Gruppe wird.

Du bist die rechte Hand des Gründers und arbeitest an dem, was gerade den größten Hebel hat. Heute eine Marktanalyse, morgen ein Klinikprozess, übermorgen ein Behördenantrag. Du brauchst keine feste Rollenbeschreibung, sondern den Ehrgeiz, jedes Problem zu lösen, das vor dir liegt - und den Instinkt, die Probleme zu erkennen, die noch keiner benannt hat.

Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Gründer (Ex-Harvard, Ex-BCG) und dem C-Level, bekommst ab Tag eins echte Themen mit Verantwortung und siehst aus erster Reihe, wie eine skalierbare Plattform im Gesundheitswesen entsteht. Das Praktikum ist der Einstieg: Wer liefert, übernimmt danach eine feste Rolle.

Aufgaben

Automation & Analyse

  • Reporting: monatliche Sheets und PDFs, Ad-hoc-Analysen bis in den Management- und Shareholder-Kreis
  • Google-Ads-Operations sowie Funnel- und Tracking-QA innerhalb unserer bestehenden Architektur
  • Digitalisierung und Automatisierung der laufenden Klinik: Patientenerfahrung verbessern, Prozesse verschlanken, Fehlerquoten senken, Skalierbarkeit sichern

Operations & Daily Support

  • Direkter Support des C-Levels
  • Recruiting-Koordination: Sichtung, Terminierung, Feedback einsammeln
  • HR-Administration der Klinik
  • Bestellwesen nach Kategorienlogik, Wartungen, Lieferantenkoordination
  • Schnittstelle zur Klinik: Bindeglied zwischen HQ und klinischem Team
  • Tool- & System-Ownership: Mitverantwortung für unseren operativen Tool-Stack

Aufbau- & Skalierungsprojekte

  • Strategische Aufbau- und Wachstumsprojekte der Gruppe: von neuer klinischer Infrastruktur (inkl. Labor und OP) bis zur operativen Umsetzung
  • Strategische Vorarbeit sowie Koordination externer Partner (Bauunternehmen, Architekten, Fachplaner)
  • Unterstützung bei Anträgen und Genehmigungen für Behörden und Konzessionen, inkl. Fristen- und Dokumenten-Tracking
  • Budget- und Timeline-Nachverfolgung über alle Workstreams hinweg

Qualifikation

Wir stellen nach Trajektorie ein, nicht nach Lebenslauf allein. Du hast dich in einem anspruchsvollem Umfeld bewiesen - Beratung, Startup, VC oder etwas, das sich schwerer einordnen lässt. Was zählt, ist, was du dort bewegt hast, nicht das Logo.

  • Bachelor oder Master an einer führenden Hochschule (z. B. Mannheim, WHU, St. Gallen, ESB Reutlingen, TUM, Frankfurt School, Goethe Uni), Wirtschaft, (Wirtschafts-)Ingenieurwesen oder vergleichbar - im Anschluss ans Praktikum bald in Vollzeit verfügbar
  • Du strukturierst schneller, als das Problem wächst, kommunizierst präzise und trittst sicher auf
  • Sicher in Excel und Google Sheets, mit echtem Instinkt für KI, Software und Automatisierung - du baust dir lieber eigenes Tooling, als nach "more hands" zu fragen
  • Du arbeitest mit Dringlichkeit und gehst in Aktion. Du verantwortest Ergebnisse von Anfang bis Ende, hast Anspruch auch an die unglamourösen Details und bleibst produktiv, ohne auf Anweisung zu warten
  • Du legst denselben Qualitätsanspruch an ein internes Sheet wie an eine Shareholder-Präsentation
  • Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch und gutes Englisch
  • Du willst nach dem Praktikum bleiben und eine feste Rolle übernehmen

Benefits

  • Gründernähe statt Org-Chart: direkt mit Gründer (Ex-Harvard, Ex-BCG) und C-Level, du lernst Entscheidungslogik aus erster Reihe
  • Echte Verantwortung: eigene Themen mit Wirkung, kein Kaffeekochen, kein Schattenprojekt
  • Klarer Übernahmepfad: das Praktikum ist der Einstieg in eine feste Rolle, mit Weg in eine Senior-Operating-Rolle, wenn wir skalieren
  • Breites Lernfeld: Analytics, Operations, Recruiting und Klinikaufbau in einem Setup, selten in dieser Bandbreite
  • Schlankes, schnelles Team: kurze Wege, viel Output, wenig Politik
  • Growth Phase: du gestaltest eine dynamische Wachstumsphase aktiv mit und siehst unmittelbar, was deine Arbeit bewegt
  • Gute Vergütung sowie flexible, hybride Arbeitsweise; Standort Berlin

Wenn du in kurzer Zeit viel bewegen und am Aufbau einer wachsenden Klinikgruppe mitbauen willst, bewirb dich. Ein paar Sätze, warum gerade du, reichen - wir achten auf Substanz, nicht auf Form.

title: Founding Account Executive – Italy
descriptionHtml:
About Tacto

Tacto builds Industrial AI for procurement in manufacturing. Built for industrial complexity, designed to optimize every procurement decision.

Over 50% of a product’s cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world.

  • 400+ procurement organizations work with Tacto

  • ~110 people on the team in Munich

  • €50M+ raised, led by Sequoia and Index Ventures, with Cherry Ventures, UVC Partners and others

Our mission at Tacto

We make industry stronger.

Manufacturing is the backbone of the European economy, and supply chains are its biggest challenge. Yet procurement in many companies still runs on Excel and legacy systems. With AI, we are fundamentally changing how manufacturers buy: measurably lower material costs and far less manual work.

Your role

You open Italy for Tacto and win the first customers that everything else builds on.

Why this role exists

Tacto is the category leader for procurement in DACH manufacturing. We have strong product-market fit and a proven playbook, and now we are taking it into the rest of Europe. Italy is one of our expansion markets. It has a broad industrial base, from automotive suppliers to machinery and food production, and the category is still wide open there. That’s where you come in: you take the market and build it from the ground up. You research the market, find what resonates and win the first customers and reference logos. What you learn becomes the blueprint for how Tacto grows in Italy from there.

Why your role matters

  • A real greenfield. You have the freedom to shape how Tacto wins in your market, from the ICP to the first reference logos.

  • You’re not starting alone. A stellar expansion team is your sparring partner, and proven sales assets and a tested approach from DACH are your foundation.

  • You write the blueprint. What works in your first deals becomes the playbook for everyone who follows you in Italy.

  • You shape how Tacto goes international. Your insights go straight to Product, Marketing and Leadership.

What this role is and isn’t

  • Hands on: You send the first cold emails, run the first discoveries and do the early, unglamorous work where real traction is won.

  • Not a managed territory: There is no machine behind you yet. You drive your own pipeline and build the motion as you go.

  • Not a remote role: You build Italy from our Munich office and travel into the market.

Your tasks

  • Open up Italy end to end: You sharpen the ICP for Spanish manufacturing, define target accounts, win the first deals and lay the foundation for the market’s growth.

  • Run the full sales cycle: Discovery, demo, potential analysis on real ERP data, ROI business case and closing.

  • Build the outbound playbook: Hand in hand with the expansion team, you develop messaging, sequences, segments and channels for your market.

  • Turn marketing into pipeline: You coordinate the marketing activities in your market so they generate pipeline.

  • Shape our international expansion: You feed structured insight back to Product, Marketing and Leadership.

Your profile

Experience and skills

  • Experience: Several years of full-cycle closing experience in B2B SaaS, ideally with complex or technical products and multi-stakeholder buying processes

  • Track record: You’ve carried a number before and know what it takes to hit it without a machine behind you

  • Value selling: You grasp complex products and translate technical depth into business impact

  • Languages: Fluent, business-level English and Italian. German is a strong plus

  • Location: Based in Munich or ready to relocate

Core strengths

  • Entrepreneurial: You want to build and own a market result, and figure out the motion when the local one doesn’t exist yet

  • Hunter: You go to market proactively and drive your own pipeline

  • Builder: You turn what works into a system the next person can run

  • Thinks beyond the next deal: You lay Tacto’s foundation in your market, externally through brand, network and reference logos, internally through the playbook and the case for the market

You don’t tick every box? Apply anyway.

Our values

No fixed career path: everyone here grows their own way.

  • We stay real: Come as you are, wherever you come from.

  • Merit matters: Results count, not titles.

  • Bold ambitions: Excellence as the standard.

  • Real passion: Grit and ownership.

  • Transforming industrials: Close to our customers in manufacturing.

  • Fun built-in: We don’t take ourselves too seriously.

  • Caring is key: We help each other grow.

What we offer

What to expect

  • Building at the AI frontier: The newest models from day one, an AI Captain in every team and no limits on what you can try.

  • Growing with clear feedback: Regular feedback conversations mean you always know what it takes to reach the next step.

  • Munich’s tech ecosystem: Every week you meet leading founders and operators at our own and external events. All events: luma.com/tacto

Benefits

  • €1,500+ learning budget per year

  • 26 + 4 days of vacation

  • €300 childcare allowance per child

  • EGYM Wellpass

  • JobRad bike leasing and public transport tickets

  • Company pension plan and discounts

How you apply

Fast and transparent, with feedback after every step.

  1. Intro call with our Chief of Staff

  2. Deep dive with our Head of Revenue

  3. Get-to-know call with the AE you’d be working alongside

  4. Onsite interview incl. case study and team meetings

Equal opportunity and data protection

Tacto is an equal opportunity employer. We offer everyone the same opportunities regardless of ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability or gender identity.

Please do not send us any personal data revealing your ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs or trade union membership, and no data about your health or sexual orientation.

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

What We Offer

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have:

  • Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success

  • Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

  • Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

  • Time off: 26 + 4 vacation days per year (4 fixed “company rest days”) as well as regular off-sites and team events

  • Health: Wellpass membership, of course, a fruit basket (!), and access to Jobrad, for your health

  • Family & Social Security: Voluntary pension contribution, voluntary KITA subsidy for your children

Tacto is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, or gender identity. Please do not submit personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, data concerning your health, or data concerning your sexual orientation.

title: Founding Customer Success Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The Role

We are hiring a Founding Customer Success Lead/Manager for the UK market.

This is a high-ownership role for someone who wants to build a market and a function, not simply manage a book of business or an expansion. You will work with some of our most strategic customers, helping them move from initial experimentation to broad, measurable adoption of AI across their organizations.

You will own the full customer journey, from executive alignment and implementation through long-term adoption, value realization, renewal, and expansion. You will build trusted relationships with C-level and VP-level leaders, help customers navigate the organizational change that comes with adopting AI, and turn successful customer outcomes into a repeatable Customer Success motion from our London HQ.

As our first senior Customer Success leader based at the London HQ, you will help define how Dust serves customers from the office. You will create playbooks, establish operating rhythms, shape our approach to executive engagement, and feed what you learn back into the wider Customer Success, Sales, Product, and Deployment teams.

Dust is an AI-native company, and that changes what Customer Success can look like. You will help customers understand how AI can reshape their work while using AI to make your own practice more effective, scalable, and precise.

This role is suited to someone who combines executive presence with a strong builder's mindset. You should be comfortable operating without a finished playbook, making decisions with incomplete information, and taking responsibility for outcomes from beginning to end.

What you will do

  • Own a portfolio of strategic enterprise customers, building durable relationships across executive, business, technical, and operational stakeholders.

  • Establish trusted-advisor relationships with C-level and VP-level leaders, helping them define their AI strategy and turn that strategy into meaningful business outcomes.

  • Lead complex customer journeys from kickoff through adoption, renewal, and expansion. You will coordinate the right people at the right time and make sure progress does not stall between teams.

  • Drive measurable value realization by helping customers identify, quantify, and communicate outcomes such as time saved, costs reduced, faster execution, and improved decision-making.

  • Lead executive business reviews and other strategic customer conversations, connecting product usage to business impact and creating a clear path to the next stage of adoption.

  • Support customers through enterprise-wide change management, including rollout planning, governance, internal enablement, use-case discovery, and the transition from individual experimentation to organization-wide adoption.

  • Identify and develop expansion opportunities across teams, functions, and geographies. You will partner closely with Sales to turn strong adoption and customer outcomes into sustainable account growth.

  • Orchestrate internal resources across Customer Success, AI Deployment Strategy, Forward-Deployed Engineering, Product, and Sales to deliver a cohesive customer experience.

  • Build the foundations of Dust's Customer Success motion from the London HQ, including account planning, executive engagement, adoption frameworks, value reviews, customer education, and feedback loops.

  • Represent the voice of customers inside Dust by turning customer needs, use cases, and patterns into clear product feedback, strategic insight, and better ways of working.

  • Contribute to the broader Customer Success team by sharing what works, raising the bar for strategic account management, and helping shape how a GenAI-native CS organization operates.

What we are looking for

  • You have 8+ years of experience in Customer Success, account management, consulting, solutions, or a related customer-facing role, with a strong track record of owning and growing strategic enterprise accounts.

  • You have worked with complex organizations where adoption requires sustained executive alignment, cross-functional coordination, and thoughtful change management over multiple quarters.

  • You have successfully managed senior customer relationships, including the ability to influence C-level and VP-level stakeholders and communicate credibly with business and technical audiences.

  • You have a track record of driving measurable customer outcomes, renewals, and expansion. You can move comfortably between strategic conversations and the operational details needed to make progress.

  • You have built or improved Customer Success processes, playbooks, or operating models. You know how to create structure where little exists and how to turn individual success into a repeatable motion.

  • You understand how technically sophisticated products are adopted inside large organizations. Experience with AI, developer tools, data platforms, enterprise software, or another emerging technology category is highly valuable.

  • You are fluent in AI concepts and are genuinely curious about how agents, language models, and automation will change the way companies operate. You do not need to be an engineer, but you should be able to engage confidently with technical teams and build practical AI fluency with customers.

  • You communicate with clarity and conviction in English, both in writing and in executive settings. French is helpful because you will work closely with our Paris-based teams, but it is not essential.

  • You have strong judgment, initiative, and ownership. You make sound decisions under ambiguity, follow through on commitments, and take responsibility for the outcome rather than waiting for perfect instructions.

  • You are comfortable being both strategic and hands-on. You can lead an executive business review in the morning, rethink an onboarding process in the afternoon, and write the first version of a playbook when the team needs one.

  • You are generous with context, direct in your communication, and committed to working as part of a team. You make the people around you better.

What success looks like

In your first six months, you will have:

  • Built strong relationships with the key executives, champions, and decision-makers across your customer portfolio.

  • Created clear account plans and adoption strategies for each strategic customer.

  • Established a repeatable approach to executive engagement, value realization, and expansion planning from the London HQ.

  • Helped customers move from isolated AI experiments to repeatable, high-value workflows used across teams.

  • Identified the most important customer and market patterns and turned them into actionable feedback for Dust's Product and Go-to-Market teams.

  • Created the first building blocks of a scalable Customer Success playbook.

Over time, you will help make Dust indispensable to some of the most ambitious companies and define what exceptional Customer Success looks like for an AI operating system.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

Compensation: £100K – £155K • Offers Equity

title: Freelancer Content — Social & Text | ca. 20–30 h/Woche
descriptionHtml:
Über uns

Kijimea – Aus der Forschung. Für Dein Leben. Seit unserer Gründung im Jahr 2011 verfolgen wir eine klare Vision: Wir möchten das Potenzial der Mikrobiota (Bakterien) in unserem Darm gezielt nutzen für ein längeres und gesünderes Leben - für alle Menschen.

Ein erster großer Meilenstein auf diesem Weg gelang uns bereits 2013 mit der Entdeckung und klinischen Erforschung des einzigartigen Bakterienstamms B. bifidum MIMBb75 (Kijimea Reizdarm). Seitdem konnten wir das Leben von Millionen Reizdarmpatienten weltweit spürbar verbessern. Heute gehört B. bifidum MIMBb75 zu den am besten erforschten Bakterienstämmen weltweit. Seine Wirksamkeit und sein einzigartiger Wirkmechanismus wurden in zahlreichen klinischen Studien nachgewiesen und publiziert – u.a. in renommierten Fachzeitschriften wie The Lancet.

Wir arbeiten mit führenden Forschungsinstitutionen wie der Charité Berlin zusammen, um die Zusammenhänge zwischen der Mikrobiota (Bakterien in unserem Darm) und Allergien, Hautkrankheiten und psychischen Störungen zu erforschen. Kurz gesagt: Wir untersuchen, wie die Bakterien in unserem Darm Einfluss auf ein längeres und gesünderes Leben nehmen.

Heute zählen wir zu den am schnellsten wachsenden Healthcare-Unternehmen weltweit. Unsere Kunden erreichen wir über verschiedenste Kanäle: über die direkte Kommunikation mit Ärzten und Apothekern sowie Print-, TV- und Digitalmarketing. Um unser stark wachsendes Geschäft in Europa weiter auszubauen, suchen wir herausragende Talente, die uns bei dieser Mission unterstützen. Unser Ziel ist klar definiert: Bis 2028 wollen wir Kijimea zur weltweit größten DTC-Probiotikamarke machen und damit jährlich über 50 Millionen Menschen ein besseres Leben schenken.

Für Dich klingt das spannend? Dann bewirb Dich jetzt! Wir freuen uns darauf, Dich kennenzulernen.

Deine Mission bei uns

Du bist Freelancer und liebst es, Inhalte zu entwickeln, die gesehen, gelesen und geteilt werden? Du möchtest mit Deiner Arbeit außerdem wirklich etwas bewirken?

title: Geodetic Data Scientist
descriptionHtml:
Geodetic Data Scientist

This is a future role. We're building a shortlist now and will contact you when it opens.

About us

Foundational is building the most precise picture of Earth and orbit, using lasers fired from the ground. We call it ground truth for orbit.

We design and run low-cost, autonomous satellite laser ranging stations. They measure the distance to satellites with extreme precision, day and night. Our data platform turns those measurements into tracking data and orbit products for satellite operators, space agencies and governments. We also build our own flight-proven laser retroreflector arrays, so any satellite can be tracked.

Our station network is expanding across continents. The data supports resilient navigation, Earth observation and the safe, sustainable use of space.

We're a small, fast-moving team of engineers, scientists and operators in London. We're backed by venture investors and supported by ESA, the UK Space Agency, and Innovate UK.

Position Overview

London · Full time · On-site

You'll turn large volumes of laser ranging data into geodetic and orbit products at scale. You'll build the pipelines, models and quality checks behind them.

What you'll do

  • Build processing pipelines that take ranging data from raw returns to normal points and higher-level products

  • Develop statistical methods for bias detection, outlier rejection and data quality

  • Analyse station and network performance, and find where it can improve

  • Work with our geodesy and orbit determination team to turn research into products

  • Turn analysis into clear reports, plots and customer-facing metrics

What you'll bring

  • A degree in geodesy, physics, maths, data science or similar (MSc or PhD preferred)

  • Strong Python and the scientific stack (NumPy, pandas, SciPy)

  • Solid statistics: estimation, time series and uncertainty

  • Experience with large scientific datasets

  • A habit of writing production code, not just notebooks

Nice to have

title: Graduate Technical Product Analyst - 1 Year Work Experience
descriptionHtml:

Atominvest is the operating system for modern private markets asset managers. Our modular, flexible SaaS technology underpins key investor- and portfolio-management workflows.

Our customers are sophisticated private equity, growth equity, and private credit firms managing billions in assets globally. We aim to deliver ongoing high-quality outcomes for them through a long-term partnership mindset.

At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

The role:

Are you curious about how technology works and motivated by turning complex problems into practical product improvements?

We’re looking for a proactive and technically minded Graduate Technical Product Analyst to support Atominvest’s enterprise-grade API, SSO, MCP and SFTP capabilities and our Microsoft Outlook, Excel and Word plugins.

Working with the Technical Product Manager and Engineering, you will help understand customer needs, scope improvements, investigate issues, test functionality and support implementations. AI fluency will be central to your work, with tools such as Claude, Claude Code and OpenAI used across research, prototyping, testing, triage, infrastructure R&D and defect resolution.

We don’t expect you to know every technology from day one. What matters is that you bring strong technical foundations, intellectual curiosity and the drive to learn quickly. With support, you’ll deepen your product knowledge and take increasing ownership of investigations and defined technical-product initiatives—combining a focus on outcomes with rigorous testing and thoughtful, consistent delivery.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Using AI tools—including Claude, Claude Code and OpenAI—critically and responsibly across product scoping, research, prototyping, testing, triage, infrastructure R&D and defect resolution.

  • Supporting technical-product discovery by researching customer needs, mapping workflows and data flows, exploring approaches and identifying dependencies, risks and edge cases.

  • Working with the Technical Product Manager to translate customer and technical needs into requirements, acceptance criteria and delivery plans, progressively owning defined workstreams.

  • Building practical knowledge of Atominvest’s technical products, including their architecture, use cases, configuration, security considerations, integration patterns and limitations.

  • Performing first-line triage of product and integration issues, using AI alongside Postman, JSON payloads, configuration data and logs to reproduce errors, test hypotheses and prepare evidence for escalation.

  • Supporting defect investigation and bug fixing by using AI coding tools to understand code, explore root causes, prototype fixes and validate changes within established Engineering processes.

  • Planning and executing functional, integration, regression and defect-fix testing, using AI to develop scenarios, identify edge cases and analyse results while independently validating its outputs.

  • Contributing to technical and infrastructure R&D through research and proofs of concept, while supporting customer implementations alongside the Technical Solutions Manager.

  • Maintaining technical documentation and troubleshooting resources, analysing usage and support themes, and progressively owning routine investigations and initiatives from scoping through release support.

If this sounds like what you’d love to be doing, we can’t wait to hear from you!

Your skills:

  • At least one year of relevant experience, including an internship, industrial placement or graduate role in product, technology, software or technical consulting.

  • A structured and curious approach to unfamiliar systems, including testing hypotheses, identifying root causes and drawing clear conclusions from evidence.

title: Growth Associate
descriptionHtml:
As Sales Development Representative, you sit at the front of how Electric Twin grows. You decide which accounts deserve our attention, get us into rooms with the people who run insights, brand and strategy at large organisations, and hand the sales team conversations worth having.

You'll report into Sales with a dotted line into Marketing. Lead generation comes from Marketing, so there is a steady flow of inbound interest, event contacts and campaign responses to work. Your job is to turn that flow, plus your own account research and outbound, into qualified meetings that convert.

This is a broad remit for an Growth Associate. You won't just be working a queue. You'll own the territory map, decide where the effort goes, and build the outbound systems that make the next quarter easier than the last.

It suits someone early in a sales career who is genuinely curious about how large organisations make decisions, comfortable writing to senior people, and organised enough to run a patch rather than react to whatever lands in the inbox.

What You'll Do

  • Own the TAM map. Build and maintain our view of the total addressable market: who fits the ICP, how many of them there are, and where the concentration sits by sector, geography and company size. Keep it current as the product and the category move. This is the document the rest of GTM plans against.

    Identify and work focus accounts for ABM. Choose the named accounts worth a coordinated push. Research the buying group inside each one: who owns insights, who owns the budget, who feels the pain. Work with Marketing to sequence air cover and outbound so an account hears from us in a joined-up way. You will also own the ABM motion, ensuring the demand we drive on top of the funnel by sector is harnessed downstream and turned into leads. 

    Map signals to the funnel. Define the signals that tell us an account is in motion: leadership changes in insights or brand, hiring patterns, funding, agency reviews, content engagement, event attendance, competitor mentions. Then map those signals onto the funnel so we know where our ABM accounts sit and how they move through the funnel. You will co-ordinate with our growth lead to execute focused ABM campaigns for those insights. An account that has read one blog post needs something different from one whose Head of Insights has just downloaded the accuracy whitepaper. Getting that routing right is what ensures we deliver relevance at scale.

     

    Run outbound that sounds like a person. Build and run multichannel sequences across email, Lemlist, LinkedIn and phone. Write plainly, in first person, with a real reason for the message and a low-stakes ask. Test angles, track what earns replies, and retire what doesn't.

    Turn events into pipeline. Work with Marketing on the conferences, roundtables and industry events we attend. Build the target invite list, run pre-event outreach to book meetings into the diary, work the room on the day, and drive the follow-up afterwards so every conversation is logged and progressed. Events only pay back if someone owns the week after them.

    Set up and qualify meetings. Run first conversations that establish whether there is a real problem, a budget, a timeline and a route to a decision. Qualify honestly, including out. A well-reasoned disqualification is worth more to the team than a meeting that wastes an AE's afternoon.

    Hand over properly. Brief the AE before every meeting: what the account does, what triggered the conversation, who is in the room, what they said, and what good looks like from here. Stay close after handover so nothing stalls in the gap.

    Keep HubSpot clean. Log activity, maintain accurate contact and account records, and keep pipeline stages honest. Our forecasting, our signal routing and our marketing attribution all rest on what you enter.

    Close the loop with Marketing. You'll hear objections, language and competitor mentions before anyone else. Feed that back so campaigns, content and messaging reflect what the market is actually saying. Flag which sources produce meetings that convert and which produce noise.

Tools you'll use

  • We run a full AI stack and we expect whoever takes this role to get properly fluent in it, then push it further than we have.

    HubSpot for CRM, pipeline and reporting. Clay for enrichment, list building and capturing the signals that drive account routing. lemlist and Instantly for outbound sequencing and deliverability. n8n and similar workflow automation for joining the stack together so data moves without anyone copying it by hand. Claude Code for building your own tooling: research agents, enrichment scripts, briefing generators, whatever removes the repetitive part of the job.

    We'd rather hire someone who reads the docs and builds the automation than someone who arrives already knowing every logo on that list.

Your First Sixth Months

  • Month one. Learn the product properly. You get to know our ICP and sit in on customer calls and demos. You get  to know the current pipeline, the stack, and the ABM accounts already in motion.

    Months two and three. Deliver the first version of the TAM map and a shortlist of ABM focus accounts. Agree the signal set with Marketing and get the first routing rules live. Start running outbound sequences and booking qualified meetings. Own follow-up for at least one event end to end.

    Months four to six. Hit a consistent monthly meeting target. Have a repeatable outbound motion that isn't dependent on you improvising each week, signal routing running automatically rather than manually, and a clear view of which segments and messages convert.

What You'll Bring

  • Above everything, we're looking for a fast learner and a systems thinker. Someone who sees a task done three times by hand and builds the workflow that removes it, who is comfortable picking up an unfamiliar tool and having it working by the end of the week, and who thinks in terms of the whole funnel rather than their own inbox. The stack is only as good as the person wiring it together, and the right hire will take it several steps beyond where we've got it.

    Beyond that: you should be able to think about a market, write clearly to senior people, and stay organised without being chased. Some SDR, BDR or comparable commercial experience helps, as does familiarity with HubSpot or a similar CRM. Interest in market research, insights, brand strategy or behavioural science is a real advantage, because you'll be talking to people who do this for a living.

We’re a team of 28 (and growing) based in London. We work together 3 times a week because we value in person time, but we’re person centric and flexible. We hire adults who can manage their own schedules.

 

The Role

40,000+ engineers have joined Dex, and we plan to 10x that in the next year. To get there we’re building a growth engine: channels, tools and agents that find the right engineers and get better every week. This role helps build and run it.

It’s a broad role on the candidate side of Dex. One week you might launch a new acquisition channel. The next you might build a lead magnet, run a test on the website or ship a free tool like our engineer salary benchmark. What ties it together is systems: you’ll build the automations, agents and reporting that let a small team do the work of a much bigger one.

You’ll learn growth from people who have done it before. Rob, our Head of Growth, led product growth at Cleo, and Luca, our Growth Lead, has built large B2B go-to-market teams. You’ll work directly with both of them, alongside Dex’s founding team, and see up close how a growth team gets built. Dex is AI-first: agents run our growth channels, our weekly reports are automated, and everyone here builds with Claude. You’ll work the same way from your first week.

It’s for someone early in their career who is technical, commercially minded and wants to start a company one day. You don’t need growth experience. You need to think in systems, stay comfortable when nobody has defined the problem yet, and want more ownership than most companies would give you this early.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own part of the growth engine: take on whole areas of how engineers find and join Dex, with targets for good candidates and the freedom to decide how to hit them.

  • Build with AI: create the agents, automations and internal tools that take manual work off the team, and help work out how an AI-first growth team should run.

  • Scale our acquisition channels: run and improve channels across paid, the jobs feed and creators. You’ll be hands-on in each one, finding what limits it and fixing it.

  • Launch new channels: take a channel from first idea to a working system, test it against our own quality numbers and tell us plainly whether to scale it or stop.

  • Build tools and lead magnets: ship free tools and resources that help engineers with their careers and bring them to Dex.

  • Run website tests: design and run experiments on our site and landing pages, and make the winners the default.

  • Own the numbers: build the reporting that shows what’s working across channels, and use it to decide where we put time and budget next.

What We’re Looking For

  • Technical and fluent in AI: you build with AI tools every day and can turn an idea into a working script, automation or agent. Ideally you have a computer science or other technical degree or master’s.

  • Commercially driven: you care what something cost and what it returned, and you’d rather switch a channel off than defend one that isn’t working.

  • A systems thinker: when you solve a problem you build the thing that solves it every time, so nobody has to do it by hand again.

  • Comfort in ambiguity: you can take a goal with no brief, work out what the real problem is and make progress without waiting to be told how.

  • A self-starter: you find the next thing to do without being asked, and you finish what you start.

  • Startup experience: you’ve worked at an early-stage company, in a founders associate role or on something of your own, so you know how little gets handed to you.

  • Ambition to found something: you want to start or run a company one day, and you want the ownership now that gets you there.

Why Join Now

The growth team is 4 people and the plan is to 10x, so there is more to build than there are people to build it. You’ll get real ownership and broad scope early, direct time with the people running growth, and a close view of how an AI-first company builds a team.

We’re open on backgrounds. If you have the raw ingredients and have excelled where you are now, we want to hear from you, even if you don’t tick every box.

 

What We Offer

  • Above market salary - we’re building a world class team and believe pay should match that ambition

  • Significant equity — we want this to be the last job you ‘have’ to take

  • Full private healthcare & dental — because life happens and we want to support you

  • Fertility benefits & enhanced parental support

  • Gym membership & wellness benefits

  • Claude tokens — lots and lots of Claude tokens

  • Regular socials, offsites and an annual trip

  • MacBook Pro + team kit

  • “Whatever you need” approach to tools and support

Interview Process

We move quickly and with conviction. Broadly you can expect:

  • We love it when candidates have experimented with our agent, Dex. Even if you aren’t an Engineer, you can get a sense of what we’re building, and we love to hear your feedback.

  • A 30m video call with Becca, our Head of Talent; we’ll share more about the team, role and business before asking questions about your experience and fit.

  • A call with Rob, our Head of Growth, on short and medium-term objectives and deeper questions on the role.

  • A practical task to better understand how you work, completed offline and reviewed by the team.

  • Onsite interview loop where you’ll visit the office, meet a cohort of the team, one interview centred on your task, another on Dex culture and values, with a final interview with our Founder, Paddy.

title: Hardware Design Senior Manager
descriptionHtml:
Hardware Design Senior Manager 

Bristol, UK

About the job

Lead the engineers behind the power, timing and control circuits that make Graphcore’s AI compute hardware work.

Your team’s schematics, component choices and electrical constraints will give PCB layout engineers complete inputs for implementing each design. You’ll help test and manufacturing teams understand expected behaviour, resolve circuit issues and take hardware through to production.

You’ll line-manage engineers, coach their development and agree achievable commitments, matching the work to available capacity. You’ll coordinate reviews and investigations, ensure corrective actions reach closure and plan ahead for tools, licences and compute resources.

Grow your leadership across the hardware lifecycle, drawing on specialist expertise rather than becoming the technical authority for every circuit. Build a more autonomous team whose methods and shared knowledge improve how Graphcore develops its next generation of hardware.

The team and culture

You’ll connect Hardware Design with SI/PI, PCB layout, mechanical, thermal, systems and firmware engineers across locations. Programme management owns the integrated plan; you’ll flag competing priorities early and bring practical options for resolving them.

Technical owners help agree operating conditions, margins and acceptance criteria. You’ll encourage engineers to challenge assumptions, using evidence and specialist advice to resolve difficult trade-offs.

What we’re looking for

  • People leadership that develops engineers, delegates effectively and addresses difficult performance issues, with readiness for formal line management.
  • Experience coordinating engineering delivery with programme management, including estimates, work allocation, dependencies and capacity, with sound judgement under schedule pressure.
  • Communication that builds relationships across disciplines and locations, resolves competing expectations and secures decisions by explaining risks and trade-offs.
  • A strong hardware engineering background spanning circuit and schematic development, board implementation, verification and production transition. An engineering degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • Understanding of power supplies, sequencing, reset, clocks, digital interfaces and SI/PI constraints, with judgement about when specialist input is needed.
  • Experience organising technical reviews, maintaining traceable design records and ensuring investigations and corrective actions reach a clear conclusion.

While we have outlined a set of requirements, we value transferable skills and diverse experiences. We also welcome engineers returning to the profession after a career break, including through returnship routes.

title: Head of Technical Support
descriptionHtml:
📍 London (Hybrid — 2 days onsite)

🕒 Permanent | Start ASAP

 

We’re Making Travel Effortless. Join Us.

Travel is essential, whether it’s visiting family, starting a new adventure, or taking a career defining trip. Yet today, over 4 billion airline passengers rely on tech that hasn't changed in decades.

At Duffel, we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underpinning the global travel industry. Backed by top-tier investors (Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures, and Kima Ventures) and born out of Y Combinator (S18), we’re simplifying complex systems to build the future of travel

About the role

As Head of Technical Support, you’ll lead our team of Technical Support Engineers and take responsibility for the quality, effectiveness and development of the function.

You’ll build a team that combines strong technical investigation with clear, thoughtful customer communication. You’ll coach engineers, establish effective ways of working and ensure customers receive dependable support as their integrations grow in complexity and scale.

You’ll stay close to the work: reviewing investigations, helping with significant escalations and understanding where our products or processes create friction. Your impact will come from strengthening the whole team’s ability to resolve problems and turning what we learn from support into lasting improvements.

You’ll work closely with Engineering, Product, Partner Engineering, Partner Management and Travel Operations. Technical Support owns day-to-day API questions, troubleshooting and the customer support response to technical incidents. Partner Engineers own strategic technical relationships and solution architecture; Implementation Managers own implementation programmes.

What you’ll do

  • Lead and develop the team. Set clear expectations, provide regular coaching and feedback, support career development and address performance issues constructively. Hire and onboard engineers as the team grows.

  • Own support quality. Establish standards for technical investigation, written communication, case ownership and follow-through. Ensure customers understand what is happening, what comes next and who is responsible.

  • Build a dependable support operation. Improve triage, prioritisation, queue management, handovers and escalation paths. Plan staffing and coverage around customer needs and agreed service commitments, with a sustainable workload for the team.

  • Strengthen technical capability. Help engineers investigate API behaviour, interpret logs and request traces, reproduce integration issues and distinguish customer configuration problems from platform or supplier issues.

  • Lead significant customer escalations. Coordinate the support response, establish customer impact and keep communication clear through to resolution. Work with Engineering on diagnosis and recovery, involving Partner Engineering where an issue creates a wider strategic risk.

  • Make collaboration effective. Give Engineering actionable escalation reports with evidence, reproduction steps and impact. Work with Travel Operations on booking and supplier issues, and with implementation teams to ensure new integrations enter support with the context the team needs.

  • Improve the product through support. Identify recurring problems and turn them into clear recommendations for Product and Engineering. Track whether fixes, documentation and product changes actually reduce customer friction.

  • Make support easier to deliver. Develop troubleshooting guides, internal knowledge, customer documentation and useful tooling. Apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, speed and access to help.

  • Use evidence to guide decisions. Monitor response and resolution performance, ageing work, reopened cases, customer feedback and team capacity. Use that information to prioritise improvements and make clear recommendations about investment.

What we’re looking for

  • Experience managing and developing a technical support or support engineering team serving business customers.

  • A track record of improving both customer outcomes and how a support function operates.

  • Strong technical understanding of APIs, HTTP, authentication, webhooks and integrations, with enough practical depth to guide investigations and earn the trust of engineers.

  • Comfort working with logs, SQL and scripts to investigate problems or improve support workflows.

  • Experience handling consequential customer escalations, including situations where the cause or resolution is initially uncertain.

  • Ability to explain technical issues to developers, business stakeholders and senior leaders.

  • Sound judgement about urgency, customer impact and competing priorities.

  • Evidence of effective hiring, coaching, performance management and delegation.

  • The ability to influence Product, Engineering and commercial teams through clear reasoning and useful evidence.

  • Comfort building and improving a function in a growing company, while remaining involved in its day-to-day work.

Experience that would be useful

  • Supporting an API platform, developer product or infrastructure business.

  • Working with enterprise customers running important production integrations.

  • Leading support across different time zones.

  • Improving support tooling, knowledge management, self-service or automation.

  • Experience in travel technology, payments or another industry with complex external dependencies.

You don’t need to have worked in travel or held this exact title. We’re interested in the teams you’ve developed, the problems you’ve solved and the judgement you bring.

What success looks like

During your first six months:

  • Engineers have clear expectations, regular coaching and practical development plans.

  • Customer issues have clear ownership, appropriate prioritisation and dependable communication.

  • You have established a trustworthy baseline for support performance and delivered measurable improvements in the most important areas.

  • Escalations reach the right teams with better evidence and fewer unnecessary handovers.

  • Recurring problems are being addressed through product changes, documentation or tooling.

  • Duffel has a clear plan for the support capacity and capabilities needed as the business grows.

Why You’ll Love Working at Duffel

We believe in true ownership. That’s why every permanent employee gets equity in the business.

Perks That Actually Matter:

✈️ Travel Allowance: We literally pay you to get out of town and explore the world.

🏝️ Work From Anywhere: Flexibility is built in. Work remotely, or take advantage of our Sabbatical Policy.

⚡ Electric Car Scheme: Roll up in a brand-new EV with eco-friendly tax savings.

⚖️ Work-Life Harmony: Flexible bank holidays, generous family leave, and a dedicated volunteering day.

📚 Growth Tools: Paid study days to level up your skills, plus a solid pension and cycle-to-work scheme.

🏥 Health & Wellbeing: Private healthcare, eye test cover, and season ticket loans.

🏡 Family Leave (maternity, paternity and adoption): Big support for life’s biggest moments, 26 weeks fully paid.

The Details

We value your ability to problem solve and build amazing things so we welcome applications for everyone - regardless of age, sex, disability, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief.
